---
title: "qresid"
subtitle: "Quantile residual diagnostics for Stata models"
---

`qresid` turns fitted model probabilities into a common diagnostic scale. The core idea is simple: evaluate the fitted CDF at each observation, randomize inside CDF jumps for discrete outcomes, and transform the result to the standard normal scale.

```stata
sysuse auto, clear
regress price mpg
qresid rq
qnorm rq
```

The same visual language then works across Gaussian, binomial, count, positive continuous, zero-inflated, truncated, censored, generalized Poisson, and pinned hurdle routes that have passed the local extension prerelease gates.

::: {.callout-note}
This site is a teaching prototype. The package help, support matrix, and benchmark reports remain the support authorities.
:::

## Quick interpretation

- A good QQ-normal plot should roughly follow the reference line.
- Systematic curvature suggests distributional mismatch, missing nonlinear terms, or an incorrect link.
- Residuals versus fitted values help spot mean-variance and tail problems.
- Residuals versus a covariate help spot omitted structure.
